# What Illustration teaches about effective guidance

The [Illustration topic](../../../design-system/guidance/illustration.design.md) inspired this method. The analysis concerns its text and information structure, not visual examples or measured reader performance.

| What the topic does | Why it helps people and agents | Transferable lesson |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opens with a definition, benefit, and boundary: art never carries meaning alone. | Establishes the mental model and an invariant before details. | Explain the job and what must remain true. |
| Translates design values into illustration-specific choices. | People get rationale; agents get constraints beyond style adjectives. | Make principles operational. |
| Explains permitted, conditional, and unsuitable uses before style. | Prevents crafting the wrong solution; alternatives make restraint actionable. | Teach selection before configuration. |
| Distinguishes illustrations from Codicons and shared rules from window-specific subjects. | Resolves likely confusions without duplicating whole sections. | Define boundaries and isolate contextual differences. |
| Groups properties and semantic token roles in compact tables. | Stable labels support scanning, comparison, and focused retrieval. | Choose format by the information's relationships. |
| Gives local reasons and bounded exceptions. | "Real words only for labels the idea depends on" is more useful than "no text" or "keep text simple." | Keep conditions beside the rules they qualify. |
| Specifies decorative versus informative semantics, nonvisual meaning, contrast, and neutral metaphors. | Provides concrete accessibility decisions rather than a generic reminder. | Select the subject's real obligations. |
| Links to Motion for its detailed contracts. | Keeps shared rules with their owners and avoids repetition. | Explain the local choice; link to dependent detail. |
| Closes with delivery constraints and an outcome checklist. | Connects design intent, implementation, and evaluation in one vocabulary. | Make the result reviewable. |

The topic supports two reading modes: learn top-down, then retrieve a rule or check while working. Prose orients, tables compare, and bullets separate independent constraints. Its concision comes from assigning each block a job, not stripping away rationale.

Transfer this effectiveness, not the contents or heading sequence. Typography needs role selection rather than a yes/no applicability matrix. An interaction topic needs states and input behavior rather than an illustration-style property inventory. Existing VS Code component contracts and user settings constrain the recommendation.

A checklist is not proof of compliance. Token references can be inspected in source; whether an idea remains clear in high contrast needs the rendered result and design judgment. A well-written topic helps that evaluation but does not replace it.
